question: Which mounted view owns widget and selection geometry, and can duplicate position stores or observers disappear?
trigger: User requested the next ledger item after Plate core. The queue selected plite-view: five architectural questions assessed together, with product implementation and publication outside scope.
requirements: Geometry binds to one exact mounted Editable and resolves canonical selection, annotation, node or keyed cursor targets.
Canonical semantic owners retain their data and subscriptions; copied UI retains popup placement and presentation.
SSR/null/unmounted targets, geometry equality, multiline/collapsed ranges, keyed locality, cleanup, scrolling and first-position hiding survive the cut.
evidenceReuse: Initial geometry ledger record, reconsidering the August decision to retain logical Widget. Current selection singleton, Yjs cursor adapter, both direct annotation example consumers and geometry/coordinator lifetimes were inspected. The historical 10,000-item receipt omits geometry and captures a different Widget hash; it cannot accept the candidate.
summary: Pursue removing the generic Widget projection/store carrier between canonical semantic owners and exact-view geometry. Keep private measurement and copied floating placement. The replacement contract and runtime remain provisional pending detailed design and matched scale proof.
alternatives: Keep/configure: direct domain hooks hide assembly but still create synthetic or adapted Widget records/stores; configuration cannot remove that infrastructure.
Change API: feed current domain targets and their existing invalidation directly into private exact-Editable measurement.
Add primitive: a narrow private measurement input may be required; a new public generic target/store registry would recreate the carrier.
Delete/merge/inline: remove Widget/WidgetTarget/resolved snapshots/store protocol and cursor/annotation adapters; inline ordinary UI label mapping into current consumers.
Move ownership: logical records remain with selection, annotation, node identity or keyed cursor cache; coordinates belong to the exact Editable and popup placement to copied UI.
Replace architecture: global geometry or merging reference and popup observers is unsupported; their measured elements and lifetimes differ.
proofLimits: Direction earns design, not runtime acceptance. No matched current/candidate scale experiment, browser alignment, device behavior or adoption run. Mocked rectangle tests and visibility/positive-bounds browser assertions do not prove exact anchor alignment. Retain historical evidence unchanged and measure the proposed path before accepting runtime changes.
